entries.content: Use snake_case for project folders/files and PascalCase for node names. Treat case-only path differences as portability bugs because exported project filesystems can be case-sensitive even when the development machine is not.
Place an empty .gdignore in directories that Godot should neither import nor expose in the FileSystem dock. Do not use it for resources that must be loadable with load() or preload().

entries.topic: Imported asset access and generated metadata
entries.content: Access imported assets through Godot resource loading rather than assuming the generated file path under .godot/imported. Commit source-side .import metadata when applicable; generated .godot contents are recreatable and normally stay out of version control.

Keep reusable scenes focused on a coherent purpose and avoid making them depend implicitly on unrelated project state. Prefer small, composable scene boundaries over one scene owning many unrelated responsibilities.
When a scene requires external context, expose the dependency explicitly instead of relying on brittle parent/sibling assumptions. This keeps reusable scenes testable and reduces hidden coupling.

TSCN is a structured text serialization, not arbitrary configuration text. Preserve resource declarations, node ownership/references and connection sections; prefer parser/editor-assisted or surgical modifications over broad replacements.

entries.topic: Serialized node references and exported paths
entries.content: When editing serialized scenes, preserve reference metadata such as exported node assignments and validate by loading the scene. If a small property changes, do not rewrite the surrounding node block unless required.

entries.topic: Physics work belongs in the physics tick
entries.content: Movement and physics-dependent game logic should normally run on the fixed physics tick rather than the rendered-frame callback. This is especially important when physics interpolation is enabled.
After teleporting or snapping an interpolated object to a discontinuous position, reset its interpolation state so previous-frame transforms are not blended into the new location.

RigidBody3D is simulation-driven. Repeatedly forcing transform or velocity can fight the solver; when precise direct state manipulation is required, prefer the physics integration callback and validate the reason for overriding solver state.

Use force APIs for effects that act over physics updates and impulse APIs for one-shot momentum changes. Repeated per-frame impulses make the result dependent on update frequency and should not substitute for a continuous force.

Use _integrate_forces(state) when direct access to a RigidBody3D simulation state is necessary. Only enable custom integration when intentionally taking responsibility for behavior the standard force integrator would otherwise perform.

RayCast3D tests the segment from its origin to target_position and reports the closest matching collision. Geometry outside that segment cannot be detected, so probe origin and reach are diagnostic inputs, not just tuning details.

RayCast3D normally refreshes once per physics frame and keeps that result until the next update. If its configuration changes and an immediate result is required in the same physics frame, use force_raycast_update().
Before assuming a RayCast3D geometry bug, verify collision masks, body/area detection settings and exception lists. A correct ray segment can still intentionally ignore the target object.

entries.topic: Scene tree access from worker threads
entries.content: Do not directly mutate the active scene tree from worker threads. Transfer data safely and schedule scene-tree mutations through deferred/main-thread mechanisms when needed.

References can be handled across threads, but modifying the same Resource concurrently is unsafe. Avoid multiple threads loading or mutating the same underlying resource unless ownership and synchronization are explicit.

Use glTF 2.0 as the default Blender-to-Godot scene interchange unless there is a concrete reason not to. GLB is convenient when a single binary package is preferred; text glTF is useful when separate resources or inspectable scene text matter.

entries.topic: Customize imported 3D assets without editing generated scenes
entries.content: Prefer correcting source data in Blender when practical. For Godot-specific customization, use import settings, inherited scenes, import hints or a post-import script instead of editing generated imported scene data directly.

godot-cpp uses SCons as its primary build system. Use project-supported SCons commands for normal/clean builds and generate compile_commands.json when IDE/static-analysis tooling needs the compilation database.
